title: AI tenant service desk for commercial buildings
description: Help facilities teams answer routine tenant questions, log HVAC and maintenance requests, and keep one record from intake through shift handover.
heading: An AI helpdesk for tenant service requests
intro: Answer routine tenant questions from your building manual. When a request needs a site visit, record what happened and where, then give the next shift the same record to work from.
audience: For commercial property managers, facilities teams and managing agents.
workflowTitle: From tenant question to shift handover
steps: The chatbot uses your building’s operating guide to answer questions about visitor parking and other services covered in the manual.
For issues such as weak cooling, AI records the location and details. A supervisor reviews the request and assigns someone to follow up.
Hand over with the same record
Incoming staff can see what was reported, the guidance given and who was assigned. Authorised staff confirm schedules and approvals.
demoNote: This simulated case uses Korean on-screen text with English captions.
subtitles: A tenant reports weak air conditioning in the shared meeting room on the fifth floor.
AI records the location and details of the request.
A supervisor reviews request DEMO-012 and assigns a team member.
The incoming shift checks the notes and assignment in the same request record.

caseTitle: Tenant request intake at a building management company
caseSummary: The management team had logged requests from calls and messages by hand. In this proof of concept, it tested a web and mobile chatbot for building-manual guidance and request intake, plus an admin screen for passing requests to staff.
caseLabels: Missed transfers to responsible staff in this sample
caseScope: The completion report covers 23 September to 22 October 2026. The figures describe the internal proof-of-concept sample, including requests raised for feature checks.
caseLink: Read the case summary in Korean
faq: Can it operate in our language?
The public product walkthrough is in Korean. Tell us which languages your occupants and staff use so we can discuss what a pilot would require.
Can we keep our existing phone line or work order system?
You can continue to take calls. We review your current channels, record fields and integration requirements when scoping a pilot.
How do we handle an emergency?
Follow your building’s established emergency contacts and procedures for fire, safety incidents or other urgent situations.
contactText: Tell us which building workflow you want to review. We’ll arrange the online demo by email.
quoteText: We quote setup and ongoing support per project after reviewing the number of buildings, their operating manuals, integration requirements and support scope.
